cells.tense: You are seeing the shape of what is here while you stand under its weight.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Follow a page, an account or an argument past the point where it gets comfortable, down to the place your grip runs out on it, and write the line where it stopped. Then set it down.
cells.core:
You can hold a hard thing and keep looking at it at the same time. The weight does not make you look away, which is why you get there first — you see what a situation is made of while it is still pressing on you. The clarity lands on something solid. You do not rush a verdict, because the verdict was never what held you up.

Take something you keep going back to — an account, a page, an argument — and follow it past the point where it gets comfortable, toward the place your grip runs out. Not toward an answer. Toward the edge, which you will feel before you can name it. Write the line where it stopped, then set it down. Today has room for this much. That much is real, and it is enough.
cells.sheetLine: You can look hard at a thing and still hold your ground.
cells.verb: catching the first clear edge of a thing before it has a name
cells.place: where you stay steady under what you are carrying

cells.tense: You will read the next scene before anyone has written it down.
cells.act: let what was only possible stand finished
cells.ask: Retire something you keep re-opening — a draft, an old argument, an exchange you replay — at whatever size it reached today, with no last pass and no final look.
cells.core:
Your eye is fast, and it has gotten faster than the pace of what you are looking at. You clock the shift in a voice mid-sentence, you see how the meeting goes before it starts, you mark the turn before it is due. That speed has been getting you through. These days it runs ahead of what is actually there, so you are meeting something that has not turned up yet.

What settles it: finish a thing at the size it reached. Take whatever you keep re-opening — a draft, an old argument, the exchange you replay on the walk home — and retire it today exactly as it stands. No last pass, no final look. You already read it. Let that much be the end, and point yourself at today. What is coming arrives whether you saw it first or not.

cells.tense: You saw this plainly once, and you have been standing where that left you.
cells.ask: Bring one unfinished piece — a drawer, a call, a paragraph — to a state where it stands without you holding it up. Not the list. One piece.
cells.core:
The clear look at this already happened, and it is behind you. Now you catch the shift late, after it has moved, and there is a gap between where the situation is and where you are still looking. You are not gone. You are arriving after the arrival — the ground you used to press on is not where you left it, and you are still patting the old spot.

So make one thing hold. Something you started and left half-done, small as a drawer or a call or a paragraph — bring it to a state where it stands without you there to keep it up. Not the list. One piece. When a thing you made keeps standing, you can lean your weight on it, and the ground underneath comes back to where you are standing now.
cells.sheetLine: The clear look already happened, and you are at the old spot.

cells.tense: You are catching the change in a voice before you have decided anything about it.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: Twice today, when something turns — a sound, a tone, the plan shifting — put the turn into a sentence while it is still warm, to whoever is nearby or onto paper.
cells.core:
It is already happening. You catch the change in a voice mid-sentence, you have a read on how the meeting will land, and the moment you put words to it you file it under 'obvious' or 'anyone would have.' What keeps coming from you keeps getting credited to everything else.

Meet the turn as it lands. Twice today, when something shifts — a sound, a tone, the plan changing under your feet — put it into one sentence while it is still warm, said to whoever is nearby or written where you will see it. Twice is the whole of it. When the sentence comes from you and the moment comes from you, you will start to notice you were there ahead of the rest the entire time.
cells.sheetLine: The read is yours, and you are there before it speaks.
